title: Home-Ed Club near Bath: horses, nature and creative arts
description: A Home Education Club near Bath combining horses, outdoor learning and creative arts. Small groups or 1-to-1, at the right pace for every child, with EHCP and EOTAS funding where applicable.

sections.heading: Home Education Club
sections.lede: Here at Creative Rein, time spent with us is so much more than learning about horses, creative art and the outdoors. It's about building a true connection with our wonderful horses, discovering new skills, exploring boundaries and feeling part of our family here.

image.alt: The wooden art room, with a long table, chairs and paintings pegged along the wall

sections.heading: Term-time sessions for ages 5 to 18
sections.body:
We offer term-time sessions where children can spend a morning or afternoon covering horse management and riding, outdoor learning, and creative art and design. Weekly sessions run in six-week terms, with a final project combining all elements of learning.

Each session has its own theme, with activities adapted to suit different ages and interests.

Our small-scale setting offers a rare, personal way for children to enjoy the world of horses, explore the outdoors, discover new interests and express themselves through creative arts and practical activities.

No previous horse experience is needed and riding is entirely optional. It's simply about being you.

image.alt: A blue grooming box full of brushes on a straw bale, with a bit and red girth beside it

moreImages.alt: A rider trotting a black horse around the arena
A jar of paintbrushes and a watercolour palette on a straw bale

sections.heading: Every child is welcome
sections.tagline: A different way to learn, a different place to belong
sections.body:
Every child learns differently. Some love being part of a group; others prefer a quieter start, their own pace, or simply the chance to discover what they're capable of outside a classroom.

Emphasis is placed on relationships, individual interests and learning at an appropriate pace. We don't have expectations, we don't have barriers; we offer choice and freedom.

Some children enjoy being part of a small group. Others feel more comfortable starting on their own, so we also offer 1-to-1 sessions, where a child can take part without pressure.

Every child brings their own strengths, interests and experiences. Our aim is to create opportunities for those qualities to be recognised, developed and built upon.

image.alt: Girl with a horse, looking into its eyes and holding its head

sections.heading: Working with your family
sections.body:
Before sessions begin, we talk with you about your child: what they love, what they find tricky, and anything that helps them feel comfortable.

Choosing the right setting can feel like a lot. We're happy to talk it through with you, whether you're looking for regular sessions, a flexi-school arrangement or a part-time placement.

If your child has an EHCP, activities can be planned around its agreed outcomes, and EHCP or EOTAS funding can be used where applicable.

image.alt: Two people leading a brown and white pony down a tree-lined lane

sections.heading: A typical session

items.text: A gentle welcome and introduction to the day's activities.
Practical horse care or an appropriate equine activity.
Outdoor exploration, nature-based learning or a practical project.
A creative activity linked to the child's interests or learning goals.
A review of the session, celebrating achievements and identifying progress.

sections.note: This is a flexible framework, not a rigid timetable. Activities can be adapted to the child's needs, energy levels, engagement and agreed objectives.

sections.heading: Education
sections.body:
A woodland walk becomes a treasure hunt for colours, textures and shapes. Fallen leaves become the inspiration for a piece of art.

We teach all ages across a broad spectrum of subjects.

image.alt: A path through a green tunnel of trees

sections.heading: What children learn

items.title: English & Literacy
items.text: Children write observations, keep journals and read new information, using varied vocabulary.

items.title: Maths & Numeracy
items.text: Measuring, counting, weighing, understanding time, and comparing sizes, shapes, patterns and quantities.

items.title: Science
items.text: Animal biology, habitats, nutrition, life cycles, the senses, weather systems, plants and ecosystems.

items.title: Geography
items.text: Maps, directions, landscapes, environments and seasonal changes.

sections.note: Children will develop independence, problem solving and friendships in a welcoming small-group environment. We want everyone to feel comfortable, included and able to enjoy their unique time with us.

sections.heading: Each session is tailored to your child
sections.intro: Sessions are shaped around the child's interests, abilities, needs and agreed learning outcomes.

items.title: Equine-based learning and horse riding

image.alt: A blue grooming box full of brushes on a straw bale

points: Grooming, caring for and learning about ponies and horses
Understanding horse behaviour, body language and welfare
Developing responsibility through practical stable management
Building confidence through appropriate, supervised interaction with horses
Supported riding activities where suitable, safe and agreed

items.title: Forest discovery and outdoor learning

image.alt: A narrow footpath between hedges, opening onto fields and hills

points: Exploring and learning about the natural environment
Practical, hands-on tasks that encourage curiosity and problem-solving
Developing independence, resilience and practical skills
Opportunities for movement, exploration and learning outside a classroom

items.title: Creative arts and practical projects

image.alt: A boy drawing at a table in the art room

points: Drawing, painting and creating horse-inspired artwork
Nature crafts and working with natural materials
Developing ideas, expressing thoughts and feelings through creative activities
Building concentration, perseverance and a sense of achievement

items.title: Personal development and emotional wellbeing

image.alt: A black pony lying down in the paddock, with Bathford and the valley behind

items.text: Throughout the sessions, opportunities are created to practise communication, make choices, develop independence, take on manageable challenges and build positive relationships.

sections.heading: Mindfulness
sections.tagline: The freedom to be you, and know that's OK
sections.body:
If your child sometimes finds busy places a bit much, Creative Rein offers quiet connection sessions: mindful grooming, pony observation, grounding, and space to notice textures, sounds and sensations.

We encourage children to use whatever helps them feel calm, and we can support them further with mindful walks, creative reflection and time connecting with the ponies.

image.alt: A black pony lying down in the paddock, with Bathford and the valley behind

sections.heading: What sessions support

items.title: Confidence and self-esteem
items.text: Experiencing success through achievable, practical activities.

items.title: Emotional wellbeing
items.text: Accessing a quieter, supportive environment with opportunities to engage at an individual pace.

items.title: Communication and relationships
items.text: Practising communication, trust, boundaries and interaction with a consistent adult.

items.title: Engagement with learning
items.text: Discovering interests and developing skills through practical, meaningful experiences.

items.title: Independence and responsibility
items.text: Making choices, completing tasks and caring for animals and equipment.

items.title: Concentration and perseverance
items.text: Taking part in structured activities with achievable goals.

items.title: Physical activity and outdoor engagement
items.text: Taking part in suitable movement-based activities in a natural setting.

items.title: Creativity and self-expression
items.text: Exploring ideas and developing skills through art and practical projects.

sections.note: These are intended areas of development rather than guaranteed outcomes. Progress will depend on the individual child's needs, starting point, interests and level of engagement.

sections.heading: Would your child like to join?
sections.text: Tell us your child's age, what they enjoy and anything that would help us get it right for them. We're happy to talk through anything that would help, including an EHCP or EOTAS funding.
